AuthorValue: After the gap, it is mentioned that a dependency, rhdf5, has stopped working, so the reactivity is because of the need to fix this issue.
There is a v1.5 milestone that was due on 2023-06. There is also a big spike in commits surrounding this date, likely due to the team working to meet the deadline for this new version.
After the gaps, there appear to be feature updates as well as more updates to the read me. The recovery may be due to the addition of new features.
There was a new author after the gap, so it is likely that this new author provided the assistance and support the previous author needed to finalize the project.

From the commit messages, it appears that the authors started to add more example data into the repository. This is likely why activity started up again, although the activity is much lower than it was previously.

After the gap, some commit messages talk about updating the interface, adding more features, and specifcially stating that the next version will be titled 4.0.7. The recovery is likely due to the start of the next term where a new version will be released.

The first commit after the 5 month gap was created by a bot, and indicated that a version update was needed for one the dependecny applications. This prompted a human author to go back in and make updates and benchmark tests for the project.

The database needed to be expanded, likely due to increased demand or usage and required updates. This is evident from the commit messages stating that the fleet size, vCPUs, max jobs, etc. were all increased.
A dependency was needed to be updated, evident from a commit message stating that Python 3.12 no longer supports the imp module, and a workaround was needed.
After the gap, the commit messages evidently show that new features were added to the project. This likely is why activity picked up again.
